keyConcepts.title: Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) Model & Agreement
keyConcepts.explanation: Sentences must maintain rigorous grammatical agreement between singular or plural subjects and their respective verbs, especially with collective nouns like crew, fleet, dispatch, and air traffic control.

keyConcepts.title: Clauses, Conjunctions & Sentence Boundary Discipline
keyConcepts.explanation: Independent and dependent clauses must be synthesized using coordinating (FANBOYS) and subordinating conjunctions to eliminate dangerous ambiguities, run-on sentences, and fragmented instructions.

definitions.definition: Countable nouns refer to discrete items that can be pluralized (passengers, aircraft, engines); uncountable nouns refer to bulk masses or concepts with no plural form (fuel, baggage, turbulence, cargo).

Auxiliary verbs (be, have, do) assist in tense construction; modal verbs (must, shall, should, may) express mandatory regulatory compliance, safety obligations, probability, or operational permission.
The grammatical rule stating that a singular subject requires a singular verb, while a plural subject requires a plural verb, regardless of intervening prepositional phrases.
A verb form linking a past occurrence directly to present operational conditions (e.g., 'Flight 402 has landed on Runway 09R and is taxiing to Bay 14').

An independent clause expresses a complete operational thought and can stand alone as a sentence; a dependent clause contains a subject and verb but starts with a subordinating conjunction and cannot stand alone.
An incomplete sentence lacking a subject, main verb, or complete predicate, prohibited in formal flight logs and safety occurrences.
Two independent clauses joined together without appropriate punctuation or coordinating conjunctions, leading to confusing or dangerous misunderstandings.

unit-1.mnemonic: SVO-FANBOYS-TENSE (Subject-Verb agreement, Coordinating conjunctions, Time & Tense consistency)
